spans.content: Sensing-Communication Co-Design for UAV
Swarm-Assisted Vehicular Network in
Perspective of Doppler
Qian Zhu , Rongke Liu , Senior Member, IEEE, Zijie Wang , Qirui Liu , Graduate Student Member, IEEE,
and Changwen Chen , Fellow, IEEE
Abstract—Utilizing the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm to
realize sensing and communication for ground vehicles (GVs) has
been envisioned as a promising technology in harsh environments.
Previous research in vehicular networks has ignored or assumed
perfect elimination of Doppler, resulting in unstable or imprac-
tical dynamic system models. However, Doppler is essential for
multidimensional sensing, especially for velocity estimation, but
it may lead to loss of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in communica-
tion. In this case, to achieve satisfying sensing and communication
performance simultaneously, we propose a sensing-communication
co-design scheme for UAV swarm-assisted vehicular networks in
perspective of Doppler. We first establish the mathematical models
for the effect of Doppler on communication and sensing respec-
tively. Then we analyze the influence of UAVs link selection on GV
sensing-communication performance. Based on this framework,
we aim to minimize the GVs’ maximum Cramer-Rao lower bound
(CRLB) for sensing estimates with an SNR loss constraint to make a
sensing-communication performance trade-off. Finally, an efficient
differential evolution (DE)-based algorithm is developed to find
a sub-optimal solution for this complicated non-convex problem.
Numerical results demonstrate the validity and superiority of our
co-design scheme. Compared with the state-of-the-art methods, our
scheme can not only improve the sensing accuracy by more than
30% while ensuring communication, but also outperform over 20%
in communication without sacrificing sensing capacity.
Index Terms—Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm, sensing-
communication co-design, doppler, cramer-rao lower bound
(CRLB).

A. Motivations and Related Works
W ITH the in-depth promotion and commercialization ofthe fifth generation (5G) wireless networks, it is fore-
the fifth generation (5G) wireless networks, it is fore-
seeable that the booming burgeon of future sixth generation
(6G) is irresistible [1]. 5G presents a new paradigm to pro-
vide massive ubiquitous connectivity, in which the vehicle-to-
everything (V2X) technology has been expected to substantially

eas, where global navigation satellite system (GNSS) and other

mance degradation due to continual non-line-of-sight (NLoS)
propagation [6], [7] and available anchor nodes with imperfect
geometry [8], [9]. In this case, UAVs, with their advantages of
high mobility and flexible deployment, have been envisioned as
a promising solution to assist ground vehicles (GVs) to achieve
network connection service, making up for the deficiency of
GNSS [10], [11]. In addition, it is precisely for these reasons
that UAVs have attracted widespread attention in both academia
and industry, and may help provide a new quintessence for 6G
vehicle networks [12], [13].

a crucial and popular research interest in 6G era, where sensing

benefit [14], [15], [16]. With numerous sensing-communication
applications springing up, it requires improving the performance

functions simultaneously. Nevertheless, in the existing research
on UAV-assisted vehicle networks, the main functions such
as location navigation and data communication are commonly
designed separately [17]. In addition, the sensing performance
of 6G vehicle networks not only includes the common position
sensing, but also focus on the velocity sensing and other ca-
pabilities, which could realize the sensing dimensions increase
and apply to more innovative sensing scenarios, such as coarse-
grained indoor positioning [18], activity recognition [19] and
even augmented reality [20].
Recently, many studies have shown that considering the col-
laboration of sensing and communication in the early stage
of system design, namely sensing-communication co-design,
can help improve system properties or resource efficiency, thus
solving the above problems [21], [22]. In the scenario of [23],
vehicle motion prediction based on radar perception is used to
assist in receiving downlink communication signals. However,
the performance metrics of these two functionalities are separate,
which makes it impossible to compare them under a unified the-
oretical framework. The collaborative design of communication
and control for vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) networks is introducted
in [24], [25], both of which design resource scheduling algorithm
to ensure the stability of vehicle communication. In these two
studies, the sensing errors of vehicles are perfectly assumed to
be nonexistent, which is unrealistic in the actual situation. The
authors in [26] and [27] study the control-aware communication
to promote the resource utilization efficiency of wireless sys-
tems, but their research focuses on system control and resource
utilization rather than measuring the ability to perform various
tasks. These efforts contribute to understanding the mechanism
behind the sensing-communication co-design. Unfortunately,
there is still a lack of a theoretical framework to specify the
trade-off between communication and sensing.

behind the sensing-communication co-design. Unfortunately,
there is still a lack of a theoretical framework to specify the
trade-off between communication and sensing.
As two typical sensing functionalities, velocity measurement
and localization occupy the equal important status in UAV-
assisted vehicular networks. Many literatures have studied the
positioning performance of UAV-assisted system by typical po-
sitioning methods such as Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA)
or Frequency Difference of Arrival (FDOA) [28], [29], [30],
but they only consider the static deployment of UAVs without
involving the dynamic scene and the field of velocity perception,
resulting in limited application scope. Doppler is an indispens-
able topic in velocity sensing, and it widely exists in dynamic
vehicle networks under high relative motion scenario [31],
[32]. In existing studies, Doppler shift in the channel is often
either ignored for convenience or assumed to have been per-
fectly eliminated by relevant techniques for the communication
purpose [33], [34], [35]. However, in the sensing domain, by
introducing FDOA, it is equivalent to adding a constraint to
TDOA, which can not only estimate the target velocity, but also
improve its position accuracy [36], [37]. Combined with the
above research, it can be seen that at present, the research on
communication and sensing of Doppler is parallel, and the two
have almost no intersection. Although the respective influence
of Doppler on communication and sensing is self-evident, its
unified performance index and theoretical framework have not
been clearly defined so far, making it still an open issue.
Combined with the above considerations, we shall focus
particularly on the establishment of a theoretical framework for
sensing-communication co-design, with Doppler as the point of
penetration. Besides, The above research point can also provide
theoretical support for future vehicle network design meeting
more requirements simultaneously, which also has tremendous
potential in the aspect of promoting sensing accuracy while
guaranteeing communication capability. To the best of our
knowledge, this is the first work to probe into both the sensing
and communication co-design for UAV-assisted vehicle network
from the perspective of Doppler. In the longer term, the frame-
work of sensing-communication co-design may be applied to
the integration of vehicles and other smart devices in the future
vehicle networks [38], which also be expected to bring a new
paradigm for the key technology of the future wireless networks
design.
B. Main Contributions
In this article, a Doppler-oriented sensing-communication
co-design scheme is proposed to improve the sensing accuracy
of UAV-assisted vehicle networks while ensuring GVs’ com-
munication requirements. To further evaluate the performance
of the proposed design, we do comparison simulations with
benchmark methods at different functional levels, including
sensing and communication aspects respectively. In particular,
the communication and sensing metrics derived from Doppler
respectively are applied to the optimization problem of the
proposed framework. Specifically, the main contributions of our
research can be elaborated on as follows.
1) We consider a practical UAV swarm-assisted vehicle net-
work consisting of multiple low-altitude UAVs and a ter-
restrial base station (BS) to provide network connectivity
services for GVs in city canyon environments, which is a
realistic dynamic three-dimensional (3-D) time slice with
instantaneous coordinates and velocity vectors.
2) We take the Doppler in the network UAV-GV links as the
breakthrough point and derive the mathematical models of
the influence on the communication and sensing respec-
tively.
3) We use two Doppler-based performance indicators ob-
tained in 2) to construct the theoretical framework of
sensing-communication trade-off and form related opti-
mization problems.
4) We propose a differential evolution (DE)-based approach
according to the optimization problem formed in 3). Fur-
ther, we compare and analyze the proposed design with
benchmark methods under the consideration of sensing
and communication functional levels respectively.
Numerical results demonstrate the proposed DE-based ap-
proach significantly enhances the sensing-communication capa-
bilities in the UAV swarm-assisted vehicular network compared
to the state-of-the-art methods. To some extent, the conclusion
can be in turn serve as a recommendation for the practical use
of future vehicle network.
The remainder of this article is organized as follows. The
system model of the proposed UAV swarm-assisted vehicular
network is introduced in Section II. Section III presents the
Doppler-oriented sensing-communication framework and forms
related optimization problems in detail. Section IV proposes
the DE-based approach to slove the optimization problems in
Section III. Section V provides numerical results to demon-
strate the feasibility and superiority of the proposed algorithm
in sensing-communication performance trade-off. Finally, the
concluding remarks are drawn in Section VI.

II. SYSTEM MODEL
In this article, as shown in Fig. 1, we consider a typical urban
canyon scenario, where multiple GVs are waiting for services
such as communication and sensing to be implemented utilizing
aerial UAV swarm. In such scenario, conventional technologies
such as GNSS systems and terrestrial cellular-based position-
ing fail to meet GVs’ location requirements due to building
blockage [39]. The considered UAV swarm-assisted vehicular
network consists of M moving low-altitude UAV platforms as
aerial anchor nodes and K moving GVs. As an aerial reference
station, ARS is directly connected with the BSs to achieve
accurate self-positioning. In addition, ARS can assist the UAV
swarm to achieve self-positioning through providing absolute
measurements, which can cover a larger signal blind to provide
sensing-communication services for multiple GVs. We assume
that the whole UAV swarm is deployed at the edge of the studied
vehicle network, and it has realized accurate self-positioning
through the ground BS and ARS in advance [40], [41]. UAVs and

We assume that there are always clear line-of-sight (LoS) paths

In addition, the altitude of UAV swarm brings an noticeable

The operation process of the studied network is described as
follows. Preliminaries: The UAVs have the ability to transmit
or receive signals exclusively for communication or sensing
purposes, and the GVs are also capable of receiving the corre-
sponding signals [29]. Step 1: By utilizing the signals received
from a certain number of the UAV anchors, each GV obtains
the TDOA and FDOA estimations and relevant channel quality
information. Step 2: Each GV estimates its position and velocity
and receives the downlink data through the air-to-ground (A2G)
channel by utilizing the multilateral localization algorithm and
the information obtained in Step 1 [42].
